title: `fsum` and `favg` of an infinity and finite values: NaN at 2.0.0, the infinity at 2.0.1
verdict: `fsum` and `favg` of one kind of infinity with finite values give that infinity at 2.0.1, grouped and over a window; at 2.0.0 they gave NaN once a finite value followed the infinity; both infinities still give NaN
description: The observation `sum-avg-infinities` (`engines/duckdb/replay/probes.json`) over a table of 9 rows: `fsum` and `favg` of a group of `+inf` and `1.0` give NaN at 2.0.0 and `inf` at 2.0.1; of `-inf` and `1.0`, NaN and `-inf`; the window frames `w1` to `w7` the same. `sum` and `avg` are unchanged (the infinity at both versions), `+inf` with `-inf` still gives NaN at every function, and finite groups are unchanged.

The change is value-side (D70) and narrows the row: `duckdb-nonfinite-aggregates` recorded a NaN where IEEE gives none (Kahan's error term `inf - inf`), which `nan_creation`'s DuckDB choice allows; 2.0.1 gives the infinity, which is the correctly rounded sum the reference gives. Both values are inside the row's allowed set, so the profile stays a sound bound at both versions; a verified plan that reads an `fsum` of an infinity gets the reference's value at 2.0.1 and may get NaN at 2.0.0.
reference: `AggFn.fsum` gives the correctly rounded sum: an infinity and finite values sum to the infinity.
